newsitem.title: THAILAND: Banpu in Vietnamese chemical joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Banpu in Vietnamese chemical joint venture.

text.p: Thai coal and energy firm Banpu Plc has entered into a $6 million joint venture with the Vietnamese government to set up a calcium carbonate plant in northern Vietnam, a senior company executive said on Monday.

The plant, Banpu's first business venture in the country, will have an annual capacity of 200,000 tonnes and is scheduled to begin production in early 1998, Banpu Senior Vice-President Ongart Auapinyakul told Reuters.
Some of the output will be consumed domestically but Banpu also expects to export to several Asian nations including Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, Ongart said.
Banpu has already invested $2 million in the plant in Vietnam's Thien Bai province, some 180 Km north of Hanoi. The Vietnamese have so far invested $1 million in the 25 year concession, he said.

The joint venture company will borrow a further $3 million to invest in the project, most probably from Bangkok Bank Plc in Hanoi, Siam City Bank Plc in Ho Chi Minh city and from an unspecified Vietnamese bank, he said.
"Earnings from exports are estimated at $4 million in the first year, and we expect to eventually earn between $8-10 million in following years," Ongart told Reuters.
Calcium carbonate is used for coating paper and as an additive in paints and petrochemicals.
